name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Do weekly automated scans of all prompts using exact string matching to flag duplicates. This catches exact copies faster than semantic scans, cutting noise in reviews. Trade-off: misses near-duplicates that rephrase the same idea.

name: Gauge
text: Exact string matching fails when prompts change slightly—like adding a comma or a space. A light semantic scan still risks false positives—two prompts may embed similar ideas but serve different purposes. Use a hybrid approach: first run exact matching to catch obvious duplicates, then apply a lightweight semantic scan to catch near-duplicates, and manually review edge cases. Settle it by testing both methods on a sample of prompts and measuring false positives and false negatives.
